book_title: The Third Epistle of John the Apostle.

verses.text: <sc>THE</sc> Seniour to Gaius the deerest, whom I loue in truth.
My deerest, concerning al thinges I make my praier that thou proceede prosperously, and fare vvel, as thy soule doth prosperously.
I vvas exceding glad vvhen the brethren came, and gaue testimonie to thy truth, euen as thou vvalkest in truth.
Greater <na>[1]</na> <alt>'thanke</alt>' haue I not of them, then that I may heare my children do vvalke in truth.
My deerest, thou doest faithfully vvhatsoeuer thou vvorkest on the brethren, <na>[1]</na> and that vpon strangers.

notes.text: A great grace to be beneficial to strangers, specially to them that be of our Catholike faith and suffer for the same.

verses.text: they haue rendred testimonie to thy charitie in the sight of the Church: whom, thou shalt doe vvel, bringing on their way in maner vvorthie of God.
For, for his name did they depart, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
Vve therfore ought to receiue such: that vve may be coadiutors of the truth.
I had vvritten perhaps to the Church: but he that loueth to beare <na>[1]</na> bprimacie among them, Diótrepes, doth not receiue vs.

notes.text: It seemeth (saith S. Bede) he was an Arch-heretike or proud Sect-maister.

verses.text: For this cause, if I come, <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> I vvil aduertise his vvorkes vvhich he doeth: vvith malicious vvordes chatting against vs. and as though these thinges suffise him not: neither him self doth receiue the brethren, and them that do receiue, he prohibiteth, and casteth out of the Church.

notes.text: That is, I wil rebuke them and make them knowen to be wicked. Bede.

verses.text: My deerest, do not imitate euil, but that vvhich is good. He that doeth vvel, is of God: he that doeth il, hath not seen God.
To Demetrius testimonie is giuen of al, and of the truth it self, yea and vve giue testimonie: and thou knovvest that our testimonie is true.
I had many thinges to vvrite vnto thee: but I vvould not by inke and penne vvrite to thee.
But I hope forthvvith to see thee, and vve vvil speake mouth to mouth. Peace be to thee. The freendes salute thee. Salute the freendes by name.

chapters.summary: He commendeth Gaius, for continuing in the truth, and for susteining or succouring true preachers, 9 noting Diótrepes for the contrarie, and praising Demétrius.
